MEM-1.name: Google sign-in
MEM-1.summary: Members sign in with Google; only allowlisted emails get in, others see an access-denied page.

MEM-2.name: Any Member responds to any Run
MEM-2.summary: Any Member can approve, reject, answer, cancel and retry any Run; Start and the terminal use the Member's own Machine.

MEM-3.name: Allowlist in the database
MEM-3.summary: Exact emails, case-insensitive; Operator emails always allowed; removal takes effect at once and removes the Member's Machine.

MEM-4.name: Members page
MEM-4.summary: Lists Members with status, Machine and Active Runs; only the Operator adds or removes emails.

PRJ-1.name: Enable a Project
PRJ-1.summary: The Operator picks a GitHub repository and its base branch to enable it as a Project.

PRJ-2.name: Read-only GitHub token
PRJ-2.summary: One read-only token, set by an Operator on the Projects page and stored encrypted; Projects may belong to any owner it reads.

PRJ-3.name: Remove a Project
PRJ-3.summary: The Operator removes a Project and its Tickets and Runs from the app; refused while it has Active Runs.

POD-1.name: Agent connects out to the Gateway
POD-1.summary: The Agent on each Machine connects out over one WebSocket (no inbound ports) and runs as a user service.

POD-2.name: Create my Pod
POD-2.reason: Replaced by Pairing a Machine (ADR 0006); a Member pairs their own computer instead of creating a container.
POD-2.summary: A Member creates one Docker container (Pod) with Slots, CPU and RAM.

POD-3.name: Runs on the Starter's Machine, Slots and queue
POD-3.summary: Each Run executes on its Starter's Machine; Running Runs never exceed the Machine's Slots, extra Runs queue first-in, first-out.

POD-4.name: Machines page
POD-4.summary: Machine cards with connection, hardware, logins, Slots in use and queue; one page per Machine.

POD-5.name: Machine Ready and login checks
POD-5.summary: Start is refused until the Machine's Claude Code and gh logins are present; the Agent only checks status and Doctor reports problems.

POD-6.name: Start, Stop, Recreate Pod
POD-6.reason: No Pods or image to recreate (ADR 0006); the Agent updates itself (ADR 0007). Dropped in M4, #41 wontfix.
POD-6.summary: Start, Stop and Recreate a Pod.

POD-7.name: Delete Pod
POD-7.reason: No Pods any more (ADR 0006); a Machine is removed from the Members or Machines page. #41 wontfix.
POD-7.summary: Delete a Pod and its Workspace.

POD-8.name: Measured use per Pod
POD-8.reason: Live CPU and RAM use of a Machine is not in v1 (#41 wontfix); the Machine page shows what the Agent reports.
POD-8.summary: Show measured CPU, RAM and disk use per Pod.

POD-9.name: Web terminal into the Pod
POD-9.reason: The Member uses their own terminal on their own Machine (ADR 0006); the Machines page shows the pairing command.
POD-9.summary: A browser terminal into the Pod to log in to Claude Code and gh.

POD-10.name: Workspace with a worktree per Run
POD-10.summary: Per Machine, one clone per Project and one git worktree per Run under ~/.clauderon.

POD-11.name: Push with the Starter's own gh login
POD-11.summary: Pushes and pull requests use the Starter's gh login on their Machine; the app holds no write token.

POD-12.name: Agent permissions skipped
POD-12.summary: Claude Code runs headless in Agent and Grill Nodes with permission prompts skipped, under the Member's own login.

POD-13.name: No outbound network limit
POD-13.summary: v1 does not restrict a Machine's outbound network; an accepted risk.

POD-14.name: Standard Pod image
POD-14.reason: No container image; the Agent ships as one esbuild bundle with its own Node (ADR 0007).
POD-14.summary: A Docker image built by CI with git, gh, Node and Claude Code.

TIC-1.name: Ticket list
TIC-1.summary: Tickets per Project with key, title, labels and Ticket Status.

TIC-2.name: Search and filter Tickets
TIC-2.summary: Search by title or key; filter by Project and Ticket Status.

TIC-3.name: Select Tickets and Start
TIC-3.summary: Select several Tickets and Start Runs from the list.

TIC-4.name: Ticket detail
TIC-4.reason: Not built (#40 wontfix): read the issue on GitHub; the Runs and Pull requests tabs link the Runs and pull requests.
TIC-4.summary: A Ticket page with the issue body and its Runs.

TIC-5.name: Sync
TIC-5.summary: Pulls open issues and the current state of known Tickets and Run pull requests from GitHub in the background, at most once a minute; never starts a Run.

TIC-6.name: Ticket Status
TIC-6.summary: Derived, never stored: Open, Queued, In run, Needs you, Failed, Interrupted, PR open, PR merged, Closed.

TIC-7.name: One Active Run per Ticket
TIC-7.summary: A Ticket has at most one Active Run; Dry-runs do not count.

TIC-8.name: No writes to issues
TIC-8.summary: The app never changes issue state or labels or comments; pull requests say Refs #n.

TIC-9.name: Author association warning
TIC-9.summary: Sync records the author's association; Start warns when it is not owner, member or collaborator.

FLW-1.name: Node library
FLW-1.summary: Nodes (Agent, Command, Human, Ticket) with typed inputs and Outputs, listed and edited on the library page.

FLW-2.name: Human Nodes: Approve and Grill
FLW-2.summary: Approve or Reject with feedback; Grill rounds of questions answered in one form, resuming the same Claude session.

FLW-3.name: Canvas editor
FLW-3.summary: Drag Nodes from the library onto a Flow and connect Outputs to inputs.

FLW-4.name: Typed edges
FLW-4.summary: An edge is allowed only when the Output Type matches the input; a mismatch shows an error.

FLW-5.name: Flow validation
FLW-5.summary: One Input Node, an end Node, no cycles, no unconnected required input; problems block Runs.

FLW-6.name: Node panel
FLW-6.summary: Per-Flow name, extra instructions and optional Outputs for a placed Node.

FLW-7.name: Flow edit lock
FLW-7.summary: A Flow cannot be edited or deleted while an Active Run uses it; it can be viewed and cloned.

FLW-8.name: Seeded sample Nodes and Flows
FLW-8.summary: Sample Nodes and Flows are seeded and only added when missing; they can be cloned and edited.

FLW-9.name: Create and edit Flows
FLW-9.summary: Any Member creates, edits and deletes Flows and library Nodes; every change is audited.

FLW-10.name: Library Node lock
FLW-10.summary: A library Node cannot be edited while a Flow using it is locked; edits change every Flow that uses it.

RUN-1.name: Start dialog and Batches
RUN-1.summary: Pick a Flow, Tickets, extra instructions and mode Real or Dry-run; one Run per Ticket, Runs started together form a Batch.

RUN-2.name: Run engine
RUN-2.summary: The Gateway runs a Flow's Nodes one at a time in topological order and keeps all Run state in the database.

RUN-3.name: Worktree and branch per Run
RUN-3.summary: Each Run gets a worktree and branch clauderon/<issue>-<slug>-<run id> on the Starter's Machine.

RUN-4.name: Waiting for human
RUN-4.summary: A Human Node puts the Run in waiting for human; it keeps its Slot and has no timeout.

RUN-5.name: Needs you queue
RUN-5.summary: One page lists every Node waiting for a person, across all Runs.

RUN-6.name: Reject fails the Run
RUN-6.summary: Rejecting an Approve Node fails the Node and the Run, keeping the feedback.

RUN-7.name: Retry from any Node
RUN-7.summary: Retry a Failed or Interrupted Run from any Node as new Attempts, with review feedback, failure context and a note.

RUN-8.name: Cancel a Run
RUN-8.summary: Cancel ends any Active Run as Cancelled.

RUN-9.name: Failed Runs stay Active
RUN-9.summary: A Failed or Interrupted Run keeps the Ticket's Active Run and the Flow lock, but not a Slot, until retried or cancelled.

RUN-10.name: Real runner
RUN-10.summary: Agent Nodes run claude -p and Command Nodes run shell on the Starter's Machine; logs stream to the browser; the structured result is checked against Output Types.

RUN-11.name: Open a pull request Node
RUN-11.summary: Pushes the branch and opens or updates the pull request with the Starter's gh login; no changes means no pull request.

RUN-12.name: Heartbeat, resume and Interrupted Runs
RUN-12.summary: 10 s heartbeat over one WebSocket with message ids; under 30 s resumes, longer marks Running Runs Interrupted and orphans are killed.

RUN-13.name: Dry-run
RUN-13.reason: Removed in ADR 0009: it overlapped with the editor's Test run (FLW-3), which stays.
RUN-13.summary: A simulated Run mode with fake Outputs.

RUN-14.name: Worktree cleanup
RUN-14.summary: The worktree is deleted when a Run Succeeds or is Cancelled, and kept while Failed or Interrupted.

RUN-15.name: Audit log
RUN-15.summary: Every Run, Machine, Flow, Node and allowlist action records the Member's email and time; shown on the Audit page.

RUN-16.name: Run success rule
RUN-16.summary: A Run succeeds when every Node it reaches succeeds; a missing optional Output does not fail it.

TRK-1.name: Run page
TRK-1.summary: Timeline of Nodes with state, duration and live log; logs are kept after the Run ends.

TRK-2.name: Outputs per Attempt
TRK-2.summary: Each Node's Outputs are shown per Attempt on the Run page.

TRK-3.name: Diff and pull request link
TRK-3.reason: Not built (#39 wontfix): read the diff on the pull request on GitHub; the Runs and Pull requests tabs link to it.
TRK-3.summary: Show the Run branch's diff in the app.

TRK-4.name: Usage
TRK-4.summary: Tokens and duration per Node and totals per Run, as reported by Claude Code; no money cost.

TRK-5.name: Artifact
TRK-5.reason: Not built (#39 wontfix): the pull request on GitHub takes its place; the app does not write the pull request body.
TRK-5.summary: Assemble an Artifact from the Run's Outputs and write it into the pull request.

TRK-6.name: Batch page
TRK-6.reason: Not built (#40 wontfix): use the Runs tab filtered by state and the Pull requests tab.
TRK-6.summary: A page for the Runs of one Batch.

TRK-7.name: Runs list
TRK-7.summary: Runs with Ticket, Flow, mode, state, Starter and times; filter by state, Flow and Machine.

NFR-1.name: Secrets and masking
NFR-1.summary: Secrets live in the environment; the one in the database, the GitHub token, is encrypted; token patterns are masked before logs are stored or streamed; secure session cookies.

NFR-2.name: Audit
NFR-2.summary: See RUN-15: actions are recorded with the Member's email and time.

NFR-3.name: Resilience
NFR-3.summary: The Agent reconnects by itself after a network drop or restart and resumes from message ids.

NFR-4.name: Latency
NFR-4.summary: Node output reaches the browser within a few seconds.

NFR-5.name: Durability and log retention
NFR-5.summary: Flows, Runs and logs survive restarts; logs are deleted after 90 days, Runs and Outputs are kept.

NFR-6.name: Isolation
NFR-6.summary: Each Member's Runs run on their own Machine under their own logins, so one Member's Workspace is not another's.

machine-pairing.name: Pairing a Machine
machine-pairing.summary: A Member pairs their computer with a one-line install; a code approved on the Machines page issues a token stored only as a SHA-256 hash.

agent-self-update.name: Agent self-update and Doctor
agent-self-update.summary: The Agent is one esbuild bundle with its own Node that updates itself from the web app; Doctor checks the Machine and reports to its page.

node-inspector.name: Node inspector
node-inspector.summary: See what an Agent Node did turn by turn and where its tokens went, with waste findings, suggested wording to teach the AI, and the same Node in earlier Runs.

flow-drafts.name: Flow drafts from Claude
flow-drafts.summary: Describe a Flow in words and Claude drafts it on the Member's Machine outside a Run; review it before it becomes a Flow.

flow-node-files.name: Import and export Flows and Nodes
flow-node-files.summary: Flows and library Nodes can be exported to and imported from files.

pull-requests-tab.name: Pull requests page
pull-requests-tab.summary: Lists the pull requests opened by Runs; replaces the dropped Diff, Artifact and Batch page. Picked pull requests start Runs with a Flow whose Input is a pull request.

deploy.name: Self-hosted deploy
deploy.summary: Web, Gateway and Postgres as one Docker Compose stack behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, or on Render.
